correctness.rationale: The Lipschitz interpolant F gives β(n)∈[1/n,n], admissibility β(n)^(1/n)→1 and β(n+1)/β(n)→1, with bounded M_z. The analytic composition C_{z²} sends the orthonormal monomial e_n to d_ne_{2n}, d_n∈[1/2,2], and attains norm 2 at n=1. The chain n=2^j is reducing and carries weights 2^{s_j}. Exact polar decomposition gives the first Aluthge-iterate weight 2^{E s_{Bin(N,1/2)}}. For N=3·2^ℓ, all but at most 2exp(-2^ℓ/24) of binomial mass lies in a constant-sign block; the first weight thus tends to 2 and 1/2 on even/odd ℓ. An analytic infinite proof and a finite exact-rational checker from the embedded path were inspected and replayed. No finite enumeration is used to infer the limit.

value.rationale: This explicit negative resolution of Question 5.2 of arXiv:2604.27762v1 is a mathematically motivated boundary for an active Aluthge convergence problem. Regular β coefficients and fixed elementary analytic symbol distinguish it from merely restating known abstract weighted-shift divergence. The example sharply separates special linear-fractional positive results from the unrestricted weighted Hardy class, and pinpoints a mechanism useful in future restrictions. The result makes no claims beyond this existential boundary.
